messages:
Anika (CS): Hey folks, escalating a customer issue hitting /v1/rerank. They sent a payload that nests `documents` -> `passages` and initially got a 422 schema error. After a retry with a slightly different shape they got 200 but all returned scores were 0.0. Paste of the ticket repro below.

Rajat (Infra): Can you paste the exact request body from the ticket? My guess is mismatch between our expected `candidates` array and what they sent as `documents`.

Anika (CS): Heres the payload (ids redacted):

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "best troubleshooting steps for redis timeouts",
  "documents": [
    {
      "doc_id": "d1",
      "title": "Redis ops",
      "passages": [
        {"p_id": "p1", "text": "increase maxclients"},
        {"p_id": "p2", "text": "tune timeouts"}
      ]
    },
    {
      "doc_id": "d2",
      "title": "Caching tips",
      "passages": [
        {"p_id": "p3", "text": "use lazy expiration"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "top_k": 5
}
```

Anika (CS): Their first attempt returned HTTP 422 with message `invalid input: expected array of candidates`. After they changed the shape client-side they got 200 but scores = 0.0 for every item.

Samir (Eng): Historically our rerank endpoint expects `candidates` at the top-level — items with `id` and `text` (or `content`). We do accept `documents` in a limited form (each document having `text`), but nested `passages` flattening was added later behind a flag. Which deployment is the customer on?

Anika (CS): Hosted API (api.redwood.ai), region us-east-1. They reproduced the 422 using both SDK and raw REST.

Rajat (Infra): From scanning code, if `documents[*].passages` is present our validator currently rejects because `candidates` required in the schema. We added `flatten_passages=true` in the newer spec but didn't keep backward compatibility in validation. Also theres a parser path that, if it runs but sees empty normalized text after whitespace/trimming, ends up scoring 0.0.

Priya (PM): Do our public examples show nested `passages` for rerank? I thought we recommended `candidates` for reranking workflows.

Samir (Eng): Docs are inconsistent. Search examples show `documents` with `passages`, some product pages re-use that example and don't clarify rerank's preference. That's our UX gap.

Anika (CS): The customer said they followed a search->rerank flow in their app which produced the nested shape and they couldn't find `flatten_passages` mentioned on the rerank page.

Rajat (Infra): Repro steps for infra:
1) call /v1/rerank with nested `documents` as above
2) see 422 validation error `body.candidates: required`
3) if client flattens into `candidates` manually, request succeeds and scores look sensible

Samir (Eng): Can you share the 422 body from our logs? Request id?

Anika (CS): From support logs (rid-9981):

```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "error": "validation_error",
  "message": "body.candidates: required"
}
```

Anika (CS): When they flattened on the client we advised this shape and scoring worked:

```
{
  "query": "best troubleshooting steps for redis timeouts",
  "candidates": [
     {"id":"d1_p1","text":"increase maxclients"},
     {"id":"d1_p2","text":"tune timeouts"},
     {"id":"d2_p3","text":"use lazy expiration"}
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```

Priya (PM): Immediate product actions: 1) clarify docs to show `candidates` preferred for rerank, 2) add a mapping guide for `documents`+`passages` -> flattened `candidates`, 3) consider a compatibility shim server-side.

Samir (Eng): Short-term engineering proposal: implement a server-side soft-fix that detects `documents[*].passages[*].text` when `candidates` is missing, auto-flattens into candidates, and returns a Deprecation/Warning header. Add unit tests. Long-term: SDK helpers and clearer docs.

Rajat (Infra): If we auto-flatten, be careful about explosion of candidate count (we have hard limit `max_candidates_per_request = 1024`). Also watch tokenization/truncation behavior per candidate — we should apply the same truncation rules as normal `candidates`.

Anika (CS): One more thing: customer mentioned they tried sending `query` as an array (multiple queries) and the server returned a single flat score list which didn't match their expectations.

Samir (Eng): Rerank supports batched queries only with explicit shapes: either `queries` array with `candidates` per query, or a single `candidates` set with `per_query=true`. We lack helpful validation messages when shapes are mixed. We'll tighten validation and improve the error text.

Priya (PM): Action items assigned:
- Samir: prototype auto-flatten + Deprecation header (PR + tests)  ETA 48h
- Rajat: improve validator error messages for missing `candidates` / incorrect `query` shapes  ETA 24h
- Docs: update rerank page with explicit examples and mapping guide  ETA EOD tomorrow
- CS (Anika): share workaround & test payload with the customer and offer a quick support call

Anika (CS): I'll send the workaround snippet and the short-term guidance: either provide top-level `candidates` or include `flatten_passages=true` if available. Offered to validate their payload in staging. Customer accepted and appreciated the ETA.

DeployBot: New patch queued: infra/rerank/auto-flatten (PR#4312)  CI + integration tests kicked off. Will schedule canary after review.

Samir (Eng): Plan for roll-out: canary at 5% on hosted, monitor new metric `rerank.flattening.warnings`. If >1% of requests auto-flatten in 24h, prioritize docs and SDK fixes. Also monitor `rerank.errors.schema` and `rerank.latency.p95` for regressions.

Anika (CS): Noted. I'll update the support ticket and close the loop with the customer. Also added a CS note about potential billing implications if auto-flatten increases candidate counts.

Priya (PM): Nice cross-team response. Let's also add a small billing blurb to the rerank docs so customers know large candidate expansion can affect cost.

Anika (CS): Thanks everyone :party:
